description:
A draft UN Security Council resolution sponsored by Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait is increasing diplomatic pressure on Iran over its control measures in the Strait of Hormuz.

Retired US General Mark Kimmitt says the move is aimed at highlighting the global consequences of disruptions in the strategic waterway, particularly for developing countries dependent on fuel and fertilizer supplies.

While Kimmitt doubts the resolution would pass without facing vetoes from permanent Security Council members, he says the debate itself could isolate Iran diplomatically and demonstrate limited international support for its actions.

He suggested China’s position may depend on the timing of any vote relative to President Donald Trump’s upcoming visit to Beijing, while arguing Russia could benefit economically from higher oil prices caused by disruptions in Hormuz.

Meanwhile, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is facing scrutiny after requesting an additional $1.5 trillion defense budget,
title: UN Pressure Mounts Over Strait of Hormuz Crisis

description:
Professor Rayaz Malik at Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar has spent 25 years developing corneal confocal microscopy, a non-invasive eye imaging technique that detects conditions including dementia, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis and diabetic neuropathy. 
The two-to-three-minute scan captures images of corneal nerve fibres, which AI algorithms analyse within seconds to identify nerve damage and predict disease risk. 
Studies show the method can detect dementia at least three years before symptoms develop, and diabetic neuropathy five years in advance. 
The technology offers early intervention opportunities for diseases currently diagnosed too late for effective treatment.
Professor Malik explains how technology works.

Speaking before boarding Marine One, Trump struck an upbeat tone despite stalled negotiations with Tehran and rising global economic concerns linked to the war. 
He praised Xi Jinping as “a friend” and said China had been “relatively good” during the crisis, despite relying heavily on oil shipments from the Gulf.
Trump said he expected “good things” from the Beijing trip but insisted the US did not need China’s help in dealing with Iran, declaring Washington would “win it one way or the other — peacefully or otherwise”.
The US president also predicted ships would soon resume moving through the Strait of Hormuz, leading to lower oil prices and easing inflation in the United States.

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is holding a crucial cabinet meeting, where he's told his ministers he's staying put in his job as pressure mounts on Starmer to resign. 
UK media reports say his own Home Secretary has urged him to consider his position.
Dozens of MPs from his Labour Party have publicly called on him to go - and some of them have resigned as ministerial aides.
Starmer has been fighting to keep his job, after his party suffered heavy defeats in last week's local elections.

Al Jazeera’s Frances Read has more from London.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Negotiations aimed at ending the war between the US and Iran have reached a deadlock. 
President Donald Trump has called Tehran's latest proposal “garbage” and is warning the ceasefire is on “massive life support.”

Iran’s parliamentary speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the US has “no alternative” but to accept the rights of the Iranian people, as laid out in Tehran's 14-point proposal.
He's also warned that the country's armed forces are ready to respond to any US aggression.

Lorenzo Kamel, a professor of international relations at the University of Turin, says President Trump needs to resolve the crisis with Iran as the 2026 football World Cup and US midterm elections are fast approaching.

The US president wants an agreement more favourable than the Obama-era Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), which will be “difficult” to achieve, an analyst says.

Trump’s fiery rhetoric also isn’t helping reach a deal with Iran, said Foad Izadi, an associate professor at the Univer

description:
A new wave of overnight Israeli air strikes has killed six people and injured seven others in Tyre, that's in southern Lebanon.
Air strikes also targeted the town of Sohmor in the western Bekaa Valley, following Israel's forced displacement order.
Israel has issued orders to four more villages and towns since then.
Israel has continued its attacks on Lebanon despite last month's US-brokered ceasefire.
Lebanon's President and Prime Minister met the US Ambassador to ask Israel to stop its attacks.

Al Jazeera’s Rory Challands has more from Beirut on the meeting between the US ambassador and Lebanon's leaders.

description:
Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, has passed legislation to impose the death penalty and public trials of Palestinians accused of involvement in the October 7, 2023, attacks. 
Rights groups have warned the bill could transform proceedings into "show trials" based on forced confessions, while making it easier to impose the death penalty. 
Rights groups say Palestinians suffer from physical and sexual abuse in Israeli jails.
More than 9,600 Palestinian prisoners, including women and children, are currently held in Israeli prisons.

Al Jazeera’s Nidaa Ibrahim explains how the Israeli court system is designed to abuse Palestinian rights.

Iran's parliamentary speaker, who is a leading member of the negotiating team says the armed forces are ready to respond to any US aggression.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Europe’s farming sector is feeling the growing impact of conflict in the Middle East as fuel and fertilizer prices continue to rise.

Farmers across Italy and other parts of Europe say soaring diesel costs, fertilizer shortages, and economic uncertainty are making it increasingly difficult to keep prices affordable while staying profitable.

The crisis has intensified after continued tensions around the Strait of Hormuz , a critical global shipping route through which large amounts of oil, gas, and fertilizer supplies normally pass.
Workers, farmers, and market operators warn that if disruptions continue, Europe could face even higher food and energy costs in the months ahead.

Al Jazeera's Perry Wilton reports
